project.title: AsOf
project.short_description: AsOf checks each policy claim in an AI assistant's answer against the policy version in force on the customer's date, stops answers that contradict it, and keeps a tamper-evident Db2 record of what was said and why. Built for the kind of failure at issue in Moffatt v. Air Canada.

members.name: Jay Malhotra
members.role: Solo developer: design, Db2, AI pipeline, UI

ibm_db2.connector: ibm_db / ibm_db_dbi (parameter markers only), LangChain langchain-db2 (DB2VS), SQLAlchemy with ibm_db_sa, IBM's db2-sqlglot-dialect (SQLGlot), IBM's ibm-dbt-db2 adapter, the Apache Airflow IBM Db2 provider, IBM's lfx-ibm Langflow bundle, langchain-ibm (IBM watsonx.ai, optional)
features_used: Bitemporal tables (BUSINESS_TIME and SYSTEM_TIME periods, history table)
FOR BUSINESS_TIME AS OF and FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF queries (as-of lookup and replay)
UPDATE ... FOR PORTION OF BUSINESS_TIME for policy changes
Native VECTOR(384, FLOAT32) with VECTOR_DISTANCE in the same query as temporal predicates
PRIMARY KEY ... BUSINESS_TIME WITHOUT OVERLAPS
SQL PL stored procedures (APPEND_LEDGER, VERIFY_CHAIN, APPLY_POLICY_CHANGE, CHANGE_IMPACT with a dynamic result set) and SQL scalar and table functions
In-database SHA-256 hash chain with HASH(..., 2)
BEFORE UPDATE / BEFORE DELETE triggers making ledger tables append-only
SQL/JSON: JSON_TABLE (citations and the policy timeline view), JSON_EXISTS check constraints
Views for the policy timeline and analytics
Indexes, foreign keys and check constraints, including a composite index (DOC_ID, BUS_START, BUS_END) that the as-of query uses for its start and stop keys
Least-privilege Db2 users: SELECT plus EXECUTE only, PUBLIC defaults revoked
LangChain DB2VS vector store (langchain-db2)
Catalog views (SYSCAT) for idempotent, self-checking setup
CURRENT SCHEMA and CURRENT PATH special registers set through parameter markers, so runtime SQL is literal
Native vector index (CREATE VECTOR INDEX ... WITH DISTANCE COSINE, type VANN) in a dedicated 32K tablespace and bufferpool, benchmarked against exact search
FETCH EXACT / FETCH APPROX vector search control
Adaptive row compression on the append-only ledger tables
RUNSTATS and EXPLAIN (db2exfmt) access plans for the hot queries
In-database embeddings: CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL over HTTPS and TO_EMBEDDING in seeding and inside the APPLY_POLICY_CHANGE procedure (Db2 12.1.5)
SQL PL procedures ADD_SUGGESTION and DECIDE_SUGGESTION: an agent-drafted help-centre correction is stored by the runtime user and published only by the editor, split in time at the change date
Row and column access control: column masks on the ledger's text (VERIFY_ROLE_FOR_USER, roles ASOF_TEXT_READER and ASOF_ANALYST), SECURED triggers, ACTIVATE COLUMN ACCESS CONTROL
Read-only analyst user with SELECT on six audit views only, queried through SQLAlchemy (ibm_db_sa) and LangChain's SQLDatabase
LLM-generated SQL checked with SQLGlot and IBM's db2-sqlglot-dialect, then run with a Db2 statement timeout (SQL_ATTR_QUERY_TIMEOUT)
Two fictional policy documents (an airline and a bank fee schedule) in the same bitemporal tables, separated by DOC_ID in every as-of query, with a CHECK constraint covering both domains' areas

dbt marts over the ledger with IBM's ibm-dbt-db2 adapter, with audit tests (CORRECTED implies a contradiction, every cited clause version exists in current or history rows, marts add up to the ledger)
Apache Airflow DAG with the IBM Db2 provider: nightly VERIFY_CHAIN, system-time detection of changed clauses, CHANGE_IMPACT per clause as mapped tasks
SET CURRENT LOCK TIMEOUT (bound parameter) for the runtime users, so a held ledger lock fails a check closed in seconds
TLS client connections (SECURITY=SSL, SSLServerCertificate pinning) for a remote Db2, tested against a GSKit-configured TLS listener (SSL_SVR_KEYDB, SSL_SVCENAME, DB2COMM=SSL,TCPIP) locally and in CI
Per-user API access in an API_USER table holding only SHA-256 token hashes, with role flags and check constraints; the runtime user may only SELECT it

Policy intake: an uploaded PDF stored as a BLOB with a SHA-256 computed by Db2 (HASH over the BLOB) that must match the application's, proposals in POLICY_DRAFT / POLICY_DRAFT_ITEM written only by editor procedures (ADD_POLICY_DRAFT, ADD_POLICY_DRAFT_ITEM, DECIDE_POLICY_DRAFT, APPLY_DRAFT_ITEM), approval applied through APPLY_POLICY_CHANGE (nested CALL) in one transaction, four-eyes enforced in SQL PL, provenance in each version's change note
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL ... PROVIDER WATSONX (IBM watsonx.ai) as an option for Db2's own embedder, with the key passed as a validated literal and never stored in plain text in the catalog

Monthly range partitioning of ANSWER_LEDGER on CREATED_AT (PARTITION BY RANGE ... EVERY 1 MONTH, open-ended first and last partitions; partitioned and global indexes), with DETACH refused by Db2 while CLAIM_CITATION's foreign key references the ledger (tested)

REFRESH IMMEDIATE materialized query tables (MQT_DECISION_STATS, MQT_CLAIM_OUTCOMES) behind the analytics views, refreshed by setup; MQT_DECISION_STATS gets a row permission, since column access control on its base table otherwise hides every row of it; benchmarked against the unpartitioned design at 1,000,000 decisions (asof.ledgerbench)

Online backup and restore drill: BACKUP DATABASE ... ONLINE COMPRESS INCLUDE LOGS of an archive-logging database while the app writes, RESTORE ... INTO a new database, ROLLFORWARD TO END OF BACKUP AND STOP, then VERIFY_CHAIN and chain-head anchors on the copy (asof.backup, run in CI on IBM's image)

A fourth ledger decision, REVIEWED: a specialist's reply to a held decision, appended to the same hash chain by the SQL PL procedure RESOLVE_ESCALATION, which re-counts the reply's verdicts with JSON_TABLE, copies the question from the held row, takes the chain lock, and refuses a contradiction, a second answer and self-review; APPEND_LEDGER_ROW is granted to no one

Correction notices (CORRECTION_NOTICE) for answers a policy change made stale for their date, stored by ADD_NOTICE after Db2 cross-checks the answer, the version in force FOR BUSINESS_TIME AS OF the customer's date and the correction's check; one open notice per answer and version enforced by a generated column with a unique index EXCLUDE NULL KEYS; a trigger allows a notice to change once

Routing between policy documents: one statement ranks every document's clauses in force on a date by VECTOR_DISTANCE and keeps each document's nearest three with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY DOC_ID ...); measured on a split pinned before the router existed
Clause version diff: two rows of one clause from anywhere in its system-time history (FOR SYSTEM_TIME FROM ... TO ...) in one statement, with VECTOR_DISTANCE between their embeddings

ai_models: IBM watsonx.ai via langchain-ibm (optional; ibm/granite-4-h-small by default)
Replay mode: outputs of the default model recorded for the built-in scenarios, so the full check runs with no key (anything unrecorded fails closed)
